- When sentiment is positive (≥0.25) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +2% above prior peak for next 3–5 days.
- If model shows strong upward trend (e.g., 3+ consecutive rising forecasts) with low sentiment, reduce slope by 10–20% to avoid overconfidence bias.
- Mean reversion is strong in 3–5 day horizon after volatility spikes; if forecast is >10% above 14-day moving average, adjust downward by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- If sentiment is consistently 0.00–0.20, model tends to underestimate; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast for next 7–14 days to compensate for low sentiment bias.
- For 30-day horizon, model often underestimates late-period prices (last 7–10 days); add 0.5–2% to final 5–7 days of forecast to capture momentum.
